Country.evidence_source: Because the BAS has not previously been used among a Zimbabwean sample, we examined its factor structure in this study.

Assessment of BA.evidence_source: To measure body appreciation, we used the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS; Avalos, Tylka, & Wood-Barcalow, 2005), a 13-item measure of positive body image that asks participants to rate a series of statements (1 = Never, 5= Always).

Assessment of BMI.evidence_source: Participants provided their demographic details consisting of age, ethnicity, height, and weight. The latter two variables were used to calculate participants' self-reported BMI, which previous work has shown to be highly correlated with measured BMI among samples from developing nations (Lim, Seubsman, & Sleigh, 2009).

Number of studies.evidence_source: The text consistently refers to 'this study' and 'a Zimbabwean sample' in singular terms, indicating a single study.

section_summary.extract_value: This section details the measures used in the study, including the Photographic Figure Rating Scale (PFRS) for weight discrepancy, the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) for body appreciation, and items for Western and Zimbabwean media exposure. Demographic information such as age, ethnicity, height, and weight (used to calculate self-reported BMI) was also collected. The study specifically examined the factor structure of the BAS within a Zimbabwean sample.
